subject.title: UI/TUI: session-recap block leaks into visible user message rendering

question: Should maintainers replace or adopt the uneditable conflicting fork PR, or wait for its author to rebase it before fixing this issue?
rationale: The bug boundary is clear, but the only open implementation candidate is outside the target repository, conflicting, and not maintainer-modifiable, so automation should not silently open a competing fix without maintainer intent.

options.title: Replace with target-repo fix
options.body: Open or adopt a narrow target-repository PR, credit the fork PR, and close the fork PR only after a viable replacement exists.

options.title: Ask contributor to rebase
options.body: Keep this issue paired with the fork PR and ask the contributor to rebase it with maintainer edits enabled if possible.

options.title: Replace the uneditable PR
options.body: Open or adopt a narrow replacement PR in the target repository, credit the source work, and close the fork PR after the replacement exists.

options.title: Wait without action
options.body: Leave both items open until the contributor updates the fork PR, accepting that the known source-reproducible bug remains unresolved meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Replace with target-repo fix
recommendation.body: Open or adopt a narrow target-repository PR, credit the fork PR, and close the fork PR only after a viable replacement exists.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to both the original shared sanitizer merge and the TUI leading-stripper path, making them the best available routing owner for the fix/adopt choice.
